page_title: rcmd - Switch apps instantly using the ⌘ Right Command key

sources.entry: rcmd - Use the ⌘ Right Command key to switch applications based on their name. [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/rcmd-app-switcher/id1596283165?platform=mac)

summary.name: rcmd
summary.one_liner: rcmd is a macOS app switcher that lets you switch apps and windows by name using the Right Command key, a reimagined Command-Tab.
use_cases: switch between macOS apps quickly with the keyboard
find a window by its title or text contents
move, resize, close or minimize windows from the keyboard
save and restore a set of apps and windows as a Stage
migrate from the App Store version of rcmd
summary.what_it_does: The page describes rcmd as a Command-Tab replacement that uses the Right Command key to switch applications by name. It shows window thumbnails in a switcher, a window grid and Exposé, and supports Quick Look on a window tile. Windows can be focused, moved, resized, closed and minimized. Stages save and reopen apps and windows, and optional Lenses can list tabs and items from supported apps. Logs can be collected via Console.app or the log terminal command, and license troubleshooting steps reference Paddle as the licensing provider.
notable: Free tier keeps the features from the App Store version; Pro adds newer features
Window titles and thumbnails require Screen Recording permission; processing stays in memory on the Mac
Can search window contents using Apple's on-device Vision models
Migration from App Store version keeps old settings intact
caveats: Pro features require payment; after a 14-day trial the app runs in Free mode
Needs Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions; without them it cannot see key presses or windows
License activation can fail if firewalls like LuLu or Little Snitch, or Paddle domains, are blocked
